scenes.tts: Close your eyes. Where is your elbow? You know without looking. But how?
scenes.visual: Title card: Read as Stretch. An arm resting on a table behind a screen, eyes-closed icon. Question on screen: where is your elbow?
scenes.narration: Close your eyes. Where is your elbow? You know without looking. But how?

scenes.tts: Inside limb muscles lie stretch sensors called muscle spindles. They sit alongside the ordinary fibres.
scenes.visual: Cutaway of the biceps: a small spindle capsule lying parallel to the ordinary fibres. Label: muscle spindle.
scenes.narration: Inside limb muscles lie stretch sensors called muscle spindles. They sit alongside the ordinary fibres.

scenes.tts: Stretch the muscle, and the spindle stretches too. Its sensory endings fire faster.
scenes.visual: The muscle lengthens; the spindle lengthens with it; a spike train below speeds up.
scenes.narration: Stretch the muscle, and the spindle stretches too. Its sensory endings fire faster.

scenes.tts: The primary ending, called type one A, is especially sensitive to small, rapid stretches.
scenes.caption: The primary ending, called type Ia, is especially sensitive to small, rapid stretches.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the spindle: the primary ending coiled around the middle of an intrafusal fibre. Label: primary (Ia) ending.
scenes.narration: The primary ending, called type Ia, is especially sensitive to small, rapid stretches.

scenes.tts: A vibrator on a tendon delivers exactly that. Many tiny stretches, every second.
scenes.visual: A vibrator touches the tendon; tiny repeated stretch ripples run up the spindle while the elbow stays still; a fast spike train appears.
scenes.narration: A vibrator on a tendon delivers exactly that. Many tiny stretches, every second.

scenes.tts: Goodwin, McCloskey and Matthews held a vibrator on the biceps tendon, at a hundred hertz. The elbow did not move.
scenes.caption: Goodwin, McCloskey and Matthews held a vibrator on the biceps tendon, at 100 Hz. The elbow did not move.
scenes.visual: Names and date on screen: Goodwin, McCloskey and Matthews, 1972. Label: 100 Hz on the biceps tendon. The real forearm stays fixed.
scenes.narration: Goodwin, McCloskey and Matthews held a vibrator on the biceps tendon, at 100 Hz. The elbow did not move.

scenes.tts: The biceps runs in front of the elbow. It gets longer as the arm straightens.
scenes.visual: Side view: the biceps in front of the elbow. The forearm straightens and the biceps visibly lengthens; then the arm returns.
scenes.narration: The biceps runs in front of the elbow. It gets longer as the arm straightens.

scenes.tts: Predict. If the brain reads the biceps spindles' firing as biceps stretch, which way should the elbow seem to move?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: which way will the elbow seem to move? Two arrows: straighter, or more bent.
scenes.narration: Predict. If the brain reads the biceps spindles' firing as biceps stretch, which way should the elbow seem to move?

scenes.tts: Toward a straighter arm. Subjects judged the elbow to be where it would be if the vibrated muscle had been stretched.
scenes.visual: A dashed ghost forearm drifts toward extension while the real forearm stays still. Label: felt position, consistent with a stretched biceps.
scenes.narration: Toward a straighter arm. Subjects judged the elbow to be where it would be if the vibrated muscle had been stretched.

scenes.tts: Vibrate the triceps, behind the elbow, and the arm seemed more bent.
scenes.visual: The vibrator moves to the triceps tendon behind the elbow; the ghost forearm drifts toward flexion.
scenes.narration: Vibrate the triceps, behind the elbow, and the arm seemed more bent.

scenes.tts: During contraction, the error could reach forty degrees in that experiment. It is not a standard size.
scenes.caption: During contraction, the error could reach 40 degrees in that experiment. It is not a standard size.
scenes.visual: An angle arc opens up to 40 degrees. Label: up to 40 degrees, during contraction, in that experiment; not a standard size.
scenes.narration: During contraction, the error could reach 40 degrees in that experiment. It is not a standard size.

scenes.tts: A spindle's firing carries no label of its cause. With the arm still and unseen, the brain read it as stretch.
scenes.visual: Two different example spike trains, one from a real stretch and one from the vibrator, each feed an arrow into one box labelled position estimate. Label: no label of the cause.
scenes.narration: A spindle's firing carries no label of its cause. With the arm still and unseen, the brain read it as stretch.

scenes.tts: The one idea: limb position is an estimate, built mainly from spindle signals of muscle length.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: limb position is an estimate, built mainly from spindle signals of muscle length.
scenes.narration: The one idea: limb position is an estimate, built mainly from spindle signals of muscle length.

scenes.tts: Skin, joint and motor-command signals are added to that estimate.
scenes.visual: The card grows: a large arrow labelled spindle length signals and three thin arrows labelled skin, joint, motor command converge on: limb position estimate.
scenes.narration: Skin, joint and motor-command signals are added to that estimate.

scenes.tts: So in a still, unseen arm, vibrating one tendon usually biases the estimate toward that muscle being stretched. A typical direction, not a guaranteed response. And when proprioceptive input is severely impaired, accurate movement depends heavily on vision.
scenes.visual: Two halves of the card. Left: single-tendon vibration can bias the position estimate toward muscle lengthening (limb still and unseen). Right: severe proprioceptive loss, major visual compensation; a large eye icon beside thinner arrows for the cues that remain.
scenes.narration: So in a still, unseen arm, vibrating one tendon usually biases the estimate toward that muscle being stretched. A typical direction, not a guaranteed response. And when proprioceptive input is severely impaired, accurate movement depends heavily on vision.

scenes.tts: In touch and pain, capsaicin opened the heat channel T R P V one on pain fibres. It felt hot, with no heat. Here, a vibrator drives spindle endings while the joint stays still.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left, from Touch and Pain: chili and TRPV1 on a pain fibre, labelled burning, no heat. Right: vibrator and spindle ending, labelled felt movement, joint still. Label: follow the line.
scenes.narration: In touch and pain, capsaicin opened the heat channel TRPV1 on pain fibres. It felt hot, with no heat. Here, a vibrator drives spindle endings while the joint stays still.
scenes.caption: In touch and pain, capsaicin opened the heat channel TRPV1 on pain fibres. It felt hot, with no heat. Here, a vibrator drives spindle endings while the joint stays still.

scenes.tts: One caveat. Primary endings are the likely carriers. In a small leg-muscle sample, they tended to respond more to low-amplitude vibration than secondary endings.
scenes.visual: Two recorded endings respond to low-amplitude vibration: primary more, secondary less. Label: Roll and Vedel, 1982; a small leg-muscle sample; a tendency.
scenes.narration: One caveat. Primary endings are the likely carriers. In a small leg-muscle sample, they tended to respond more to low-amplitude vibration than secondary endings.

scenes.tts: But in contracting muscle, secondary endings and tendon organs respond too. So primary endings are not shown to act alone.
scenes.visual: Three response bars, primary, secondary and tendon organ, overlap. Label: primary (Ia) endings, not shown to act alone.
scenes.narration: But in contracting muscle, secondary endings and tendon organs respond too. So primary endings are not shown to act alone.

scenes.tts: So vibrating one tendon can make a still limb feel moved. The brain reads the extra spindle firing as stretch.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: vibrating one tendon can make a still, unseen limb feel moved; the extra spindle firing is read as stretch.
scenes.narration: So vibrating one tendon can make a still limb feel moved. The brain reads the extra spindle firing as stretch.
